notes: The page continues a construction in which a degree-two map q defines an involution sigma_tildeA. The maps o and p are induced by inclusions into Y on pi_0. It presents the pair consisting of tildeA -> S and its involution, or equivalently the displayed degree-two system, as graph data: S is the vertex set and tildeA the set of oriented arcs, with o called the origin map. The text says this graph depends on hatX, while the choice of I is retained by the additional unlabeled map I -> S in (9). This describes the manuscript and is not an independent mathematical verification.

All four occurrences of the origin-map symbol are read o. The diagram labels have sigma-like exit strokes when isolated; comparison with the explicit sigma_tildeA and with the repeated closed o form on the same sheet supports the alternative o at M0929-M0931 with medium confidence. The complete systems were included in the independent-reading boxes and audited.

The second diagram has parentheses only around its top row, a downward arrow to A, the unpunctuated label deg 2 at the left, and a following comma. These are retained without reinterpreting the mathematical layout.

Both ens abbreviations lack the point supplied by both witnesses. H's munies d'une orientation paraphrases the visible orientées, and its guillemets replace actual raised double ticks. The semantic content of the oriented-arc phrase is unchanged by that wording correction.

The tilde-A in the upper inclusion is heavily retraced. Its live capital A remains identifiable, but no separate underlying symbol or independent cancellation can be isolated. No deleted letter is invented.

Independent audit: all four origin-map occurrences retain o after comparison with the separate angular sigma on this sheet and scan008. The parenthesis after arcs begins with a low short mark, now recorded as dash/ou uncertainty; no grammatical synonym is imposed on it. The complete two graph systems, the inclusion arrows and (9) agree. This does not independently verify the graph construction.
